title: Crash on KDE Plasma Wayland session after last update with "explicit sync is used, but no acquire point is set" (nvidia)
body:
### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Linux Wayland

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

KDE Plasma 6.2.5

### WezTerm version

wezterm-git-20250208.194037.a3b4d5e8-1

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

Yes, and I updated the version box above to show the version of the nightly that I tried

### Describe the bug

When launching wezterm, it immediately crashes with wayland protocol error

### To Reproduce

1. Update wezterm to the latest git version
2. Launch it under KDE Plasma with Wayland session

### Configuration

Also happens when running `wezterm-gui -n`, so don't think that's config related

### Expected Behavior

Wezterm does not crash

### Logs

```
▲ ~ wezterm-gui -n
wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1#31: error 4: explicit sync is used, but no acquire point is set
Protocol error 4 on object wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1@31:
16:58:55.419  ERROR  wezterm_gui > running message loop: Protocol error 4 on object wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1@31: ; terminating
```

### Anything else?

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I've bisected it down to this commit:

```
d1684d38e83d31dcd28dfc7dcc36ac4ba9eb582c is the first bad commit
commit d1684d38e83d31dcd28dfc7dcc36ac4ba9eb582c (HEAD)
Author: <redacted-name>
Date:   Sat Feb 8 21:33:12 2025 +0100

    Fix crash on hidpi with wayland (#6508)

 window/src/os/wayland/window.rs | 2 ++
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)
```

#6508 seems to be related

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Can confirm this happening to me too and started on Feb 8th as well (+- a few days). Wezterm keeps crashing on launch, same error: "running message loop: Protocol error 4 on object wp_linux_drm_syncobj_surface_v1@31:"

However this crash doesn't occur on integrated graphics (wayland as well), only occurs on dedicated GPU mode.

Operating System: Arch Linux
KDE Plasma Version: 6.2.5
KDE Frameworks Version: 6.10.0
Qt Version: 6.8.2
Kernel Version: 6.13.2-arch1-1 (64-bit)
Graphics Platform: Wayland
Processors: 16 × AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics
Memory: 31.2 GiB of RAM
Graphics Processor: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU/PCIe/SSE2

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Maybe this is NVIDIA related? Have the same issue on my desktop PC with an RTX 2070 card.
This only happens on my primary monitor: 3840x2160 150% scaling, on the secondary monitor 1920x1080 100% scaling wezterm starts normally.
When connecting my laptop without a discrete graphics card (integrated Intel graphics) to both monitors (with the same scaling factors) wezterm also only works normally.

WebGPU: name=NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070, device_type=DiscreteGpu, backend=Vulkan, driver=NVIDIA, driver_info=565.77, vendor=4318, device=7943

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
For me problem also occurs on NVIDIA with 150% scaled 4K display.

Just updated to the latest wezterm git version on my laptop with Intel iGPU, and issue is not present there (same version of KDE, also wayland, same display)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Temporary solution: use `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` env when running wezterm

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Possibly related: Using WezTerm (copr nightly) on Fedora 41, I had been dealing with issues on Hyprland which were causing wezterm to stutter, and freeze constantly. Seeing the title of this issue gave me the idea to tinker with a setting in Hyprland I had set recently
`render:explicit_sync = 0`
I had this in my Hyprland configuration; upon removing it, the issue completely went away.
This is fine for me as this setting in Hyprland wasn't making a difference anyways, however I thought it may be worth letting you all know.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
As mentioned earlier, this issue does not appear to be exclusive to KDE Plasma. It seems to stem from a broader incompatibility with Wayland & NVIDIA. Specifically, WezTerm crashes on launch across various environments — including GNOME, Plasma, and Hyprland — when the following conditions are met (*AFAIK):

1. Wayland is in use.
2. The system is running NVIDIA’s proprietary drivers.
3. Display scaling is set to a value greater than 1.

Additional notes:
- Setting `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1` can prevent the crash, but significantly degrades performance, rendering WezTerm practically unusable (setting `render:explicit_sync = 0` in hyprland's config file will achieve the same thing).

- Setting `config.enable_wayland = false` also prevents the crash. On GNOME, this workaround is actually quite effective — the terminal remains sharp, responsive, and scales correctly. However, on Hyprland, the result is a blurry, pixelated UI, and scaling no longer functions, again, rendering WezTerm practically unusable.
So without setting the screen scaling to 1, or uninstalling NVIDIA's proprietary drivers, I couldn't get WezTerm to be usable at all on Hyprland (even with the flags mentioned above).

I haven’t yet tested the proposed fix in [commit 5243d73](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/commit/5243d733532221b746f7921b3ac76c5193f49a3a), but plan to do so soon and will report back with results. I'm running WezTerm version 20250511-222309-475e9f57, not sure if it already includes that commit.

With all that said, WezTerm remains one of my absolute favorite pieces of software—it's an incredible project. If there's anything I can help test or investigate (especially considering @participant3 may not currently have access to an NVIDIA GPU after switching to AMD), I'd be more than happy to assist however I can! ❤️

EDIT:
I think I found a good solution for Hyprland for now!

We know we can set `config.enable_wayland = false` in a WezTerm config file to mitigate the crash, while in GNOME it works well, on Hyprland this seems to make WezTerm very blurry/pixelated (depending on whether you set `use_nearest_neighbor` to `true` or `false` in your Hyprland config file).

A solution to restore the sharpness is to set the following in `hyprland.conf`:

```conf
xwayland {
    force_zero_scaling = true
}
```

You can read more about this option [here](https://<redacted-host>/Configuring/Variables/#xwayland).

This will effectively allow us to have proper scaling for all windows other than WezTerm, keeping it sharp. However, a problem that arises is that our font in WezTerm is now tiny. Using `DecreaseFontSize`/`IncreaseFontSize` won't work because I believe Hyprland isn't yet listed in the [tiling desktop environments](https://wezterm.org/config/lua/config/tiling_desktop_environments.html) configuration.

To fix this, we can add the following flag to our WezTerm config:

```lua
config.adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size = false
```

You can read more about this option [here](https://wezterm.org/config/lua/config/adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size.html).

Now we can properly increase and decrease the font size to our liking!

We can also add something like:

```lua
config.font_size = 28.0
```

to the WezTerm config to get a reasonable font size right from the start.

Hope that helps!

DOUBLE EDIT:
Sadly, `force_zero_scaling = true` isn't an amazing solution as it will cause some offset issues in Hyprland. Though, without it we get a more blurry GUI in WezTerm. So that's the tradeoff at the moment.

After running WezTerm with XWayland using the above workarounds for a few weeks now, sadly, it's become obvious that there are many significant limitations with XWayland.

Since the crash only occurs when the display scale factor is above 1.0, I was wondering if it would be possible to add an option for WezTerm to ignore the compositor's scale factor and always render at scale 1.0 on Wayland? For example via a flag: 
```lua
config.force_wayland_scale_1 = true
```

This would allow WezTerm to run natively on Wayland (avoiding XWayland's limitations) while other applications continue to use the system's scale factor normally. Not sure if this is possible at all. Any thoughts @participant3?

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
@participant13 , imho the (multi) DPI aware scaling is one of the main user facing advantages of wayland, so i guess the project should rather be focused on fixing the underlying issue.

for the meantime you can also get a properly scaled Wezterm on XWayland.
`.config/wezterm/wezterm.lua`:
```lua
config.enable_wayland = false
```

`.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`:
```
xwayland {
	force_zero_scaling = true
}
```

Thats all you need to tell Hyprland to stop scaling the xwayland apps, but it is not telling them at which DPI to render, so you have to do it manually, calculate your screens DPI (mine is 153) and run this:
```bash
echo "Xft.dpi: 153" | xrdb -merge
```

i have added it to my hyprland conf to be executed on login:
```
exec-once = echo "Xft.dpi: 153" | xrdb -merge
```

If i work on another external monitor i need to change the value and restart Wezterm, so its not optimal but for 99% of time the problem is out of the way at least.

Hope this help you as well. :)
